title: Did Chase Bank have a data breach?
content_md: Yes, Chase Bank reported a cyberattack on a third-party service provider that handles JPMorgan Chase customers’ personal information. In an X post published on Nov 19th, 2026, Chase revealed that attackers stole marketing data from customers of the biggest bank in the USA. The stolen information likely includes customer names, email addresses, phone numbers, and physical address details associated with their JPMorgan Chase financial accounts. The New York-based multinational banking institution has begun notifying customers of the breach and is offering support, including free credit monitoring. Chase said this breach is not related to the service disruption that occurred just days earlier. Key takeaways Chase confirmed a third-party cyberattack that stole customer marketing data, including names, emails, and addresses. The recently formed hacker group “n0n” likely carried out the attack and has claimed responsibility for over 200 attacks this year. Stolen marketing data may sound innocent, but such data can enable sophisticated phishing attacks, identity fraud, and resale on the Dark Web. Chase advises customers to monitor their accounts, ignore suspicious contacts, and use multiple layers of cybersec
